headline: AutoDNA: AI agents ran a DNA lab end to end — humans did the restocking
text: Give a laboratory one typed instruction and walk away. That is the promise of AutoDNA, a system described this week in Nature: a team of AI agents that designs DNA experiments, runs the instruments, fixes its own mistakes, and keeps going for more than eight days straight — while the people in the room mostly top up chemicals and keep the machines running. The work comes from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, where computer scientist Haibo Chen and colleagues built the lab around AI from the start, instead of bolting automation onto a human workflow. In its most demanding test, the system turned a sentence into DNA and read it back perfectly after 11,382 automated steps. Sources: Nature — 'An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations' (November 4, 2026).
